entities.summary:
Zeno was Eastern Roman emperor from 474 to 475 and again from 476 to 491. His reign was marked by domestic revolts and religious dissension, which were exacerbated by the ongoing pressure from barbarian groups.

The Western Roman Empire fell following the deposition of Romulus Augustulus, while Zeno successfully stabilized the Eastern empire through a series of military campaigns and diplomatic maneuvers.

Zeno's reign was also notable for its impact on the development of Christianity, as he sought to maintain the empire's unity in the face of theological disputes between Orthodox and Arian factions.

The legacy of Zeno can be seen in the continued stability of the Eastern Roman Empire, which would eventually give rise to the Byzantine Empire.

A striking statistic on Zeno's reign is that he reigned for 17 years, the longest reign of any Eastern Roman emperor.
